messages:
nate.wu: heads up — spotted a public gist that includes what looks like a Vault service token for `svc-ci-deploy`. gist: https://gist.github.com/zzzzzz — gist created 2026-03-19T05:10Z
sam.ortiz: can you paste the token id (masked) and any hint about the role? assume compromise until proven otherwise.
nate.wu: token id ends with `-9b2c`. gist comment says used by CI runner to pull manifests.
priya.kaur: tagging sec-oncall @sam.ortiz. immediate steps: revoke token, rotate any secrets that token could access, and block the gist owner if it's an org account.
sam.ortiz: revoking now. using Vault hosted API and disabling KMS key versions:```
vault token-revoke -id svc-ci-9b2c
# GCP KMS: mark current versions as destroyed
gcloud kms keys versions destroy 1 --key=ci-deploy-key --location=global --keyring=redwood-kr --quiet
```
sam.ortiz: created incident INC-2026-1402 and started an initial timeline. will attach artifacts.
lucy.h: checking Vault audit for uses and CIDR of callers. grep on audit path for svc-ci-9b2c then cross-ref with Cloud KMS logs for decrypts.
devon.li: blast radius quick estimate: CI pipelines for staging and prod use that token to fetch image tags from gcr and to read artifact manifests from a bucket. recommend rotating container registry tokens and revoking any temporary build service accounts.
priya.kaur: I've rotated the registry creds and rotated credentials for the build SA in staging. paused prod deploys until we validate. also applied a temporary RBAC hold: removed the "ci-deploy" role from the global deploy group.
sam.ortiz: found KMS decrypts from a runner IP at 2026-03-18T22:59Z — unfamiliar ASN. adding network indicators and creating a denylist entry while we investigate.
nate.wu: I searched other public gists for similar tokens using pattern "svc-" and found one older gist in the same GH account. DMed the account owner for context; they claim it was paste accidentally by an external contractor.
lucy.h: GH audit shows file creation by user ext-joe@contractor-company on 2026-03-18T02:07Z. flagging contractor access.
devon.li: CI updated to use short-lived OIDC tokens + Workload Identity for KMS access. tested canary deploy in staging and succeeded. will plan prod rollout after security sign-off.
priya.kaur: owner map: priya — RBAC + CI short-term config; sam — revocations + KMS ops; devon — CI rollout + registry rotate; lucy — logs + forensic. rotations-bot scheduled a token reissue window 2026-03-19T06:00Z (owner: priya.kaur).
rotations-bot: reminder created: token rotation window 2026-03-19T06:00Z -> owner priya.kaur
priya.kaur: added short TTL policy to Vault for deploy tokens (max_ttl=15m) and adjusted policy to remove broad read on artifact buckets. monitoring for auth failures.
sam.ortiz: revocations complete. INC-2026-1402 updated with timeline, logs, and revoked token ids. leaving open for postmortem and CI proof.
lucy.h: forensic note — no sign of DB or secret engine reads beyond artifact reads. seems limited to deploy artifacts and image tags. still treat as sensitive.
nate.wu: can we add pre-commit and org-level GH push policies that block secrets and prevent gist creation from org accounts? also recommend alerting on public gists containing company prefixes like `svc-`, `infra-`, `ci-`.
priya.kaur: agreed — filing RFC for pre-commit + GH org policy (RFC-SEC-2026-07). will also add a detection rule to security alerts.
devon.li: postmortem owners: priya, sam, lucy. initial root cause draft: contractor copied token into a public gist by mistake + long-lived deploy token allowed too much exposure. proposed mitigations: short TTLs, OIDC for CI, GH org restrict gist creation, automated secrets scanning.
priya.kaur: thanks team. once postmortem is posted, we'll schedule follow-ups for RBAC changes and the RFC. closing incident after postmortem complete. :white_check_mark:
